acceptedSources.title: Adolescents’ short-form video addiction and sleep quality: the mediating role of social anxiety
acceptedSources.abstract: Abstract Background Adolescence is a critical period for individual growth and development. Insufficient sleep adversely affects adolescents’ physical development, blood pressure, vision, and cognitive function. This study examined the effect of short-form video addiction on adolescents’ sleep quality, as well as the mediating role of social anxiety, to identify methods for improving adolescents’ sleep quality in the Internet era. Methods A questionnaire survey was conducted in this cross-sectional study on 1629 adolescents recruited from three high schools. Their short-form video addiction, social anxiety, and sleep quality were evaluated using corresponding scales. Pearson correlation analysis was carried out to analyze the relationships among short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety. Mediating effect analysis was constructed using AMOS 20.0 statistical software. Results Participants’ sleep quality score is 6.12 ± 3.29 points. The detection rate of sleep quality among them is 31.06%. Short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety are significantly correlated ( r = 0.439, 0.404, 0.457, P < 0.001). The direct effect of short-form video addiction on sleep quality is 0.248, accounting for 62.4% of the total effect. The indirect effect exerted through social anxiety is 0.149, accounting for 37.6%. Conclusions Sleep disorders are very common among Chinese adolescents. Short‐form video addiction is positively correlated with adolescents’ sleep quality and social anxiety. Social anxiety partially mediates the relationship between short-form video addiction and sleep quality. The adverse effects of short-form video addiction and social anxiety on the sleep quality of this group must be minimized. Schools are recommended to implement measures to promote sleep quality among adolescents.

acceptedSources.summary: 本研究旨在探討青少年短影音成癮對睡眠品質的影響，並檢驗社交焦慮的中介作用，以尋找網路時代改善睡眠品質的方法。研究採橫斷式問卷調查，納入來自三所高中的1629名青少年，使用相應量表評估短影音成癮、社交焦慮與睡眠品質，並以皮爾森相關與AMOS 20.0進行中介分析。結果顯示，受試者睡眠品質分數為6.12±3.29，睡眠品質異常檢出率為31.06%；短影音成癮、睡眠品質與社交焦慮彼此皆呈顯著相關（r=0.439、0.404、0.457，P<0.001）。短影音成癮對睡眠品質的直接效果為0.248，占總效果62.4%，經由社交焦慮的間接效果為0.149，占37.6%，表示社交焦慮具有部分中介作用。限制在於摘要未提供量表名稱與抽樣細節，且橫斷設計無法推論因果。

acceptedSources.title: The Use of Social Media in Children and Adolescents: Scoping Review on the Potential Risks
acceptedSources.abstract: In recent years, social media has become part of our lives, even among children. From the beginning of COVID-19 pandemic period, media device and Internet access rapidly increased. Adolescents connected Internet alone, consulting social media, mostly Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. During "lockdown", the Internet usage allowed communication with peers and the continuity activities such as school teaching. However, we have to keep in mind that media usage may be related to some adverse consequences especially in the most vulnerable people, such as the young. Aim of the review is to focus on risks correlated to social media use by children and adolescents, identifying spies of rising problems and engaging in preventive recommendations. The scoping review was performed according to PRISMA guidelines, searching on PubMed the terms "social media" or "social network", "health", and "pediatrics". Excluding articles not pertinent, we found 68 reports. Out of them, 19 were dealing with depression, 15 with diet, and 15 with psychological problems, which appeared to be the most reported risk of social media use. Other identified associated problems were sleep, addiction, anxiety, sex related issues, behavioral problems, body image, physical activity, online grooming, sight, headache, and dental caries. Public and medical awareness must rise over this topic and new prevention measures must be found, starting with health practitioners, caregivers, and websites/application developers. Pediatricians should be aware of the risks associated to a problematic social media use for the young's health and identify sentinel signs in children as well as prevent negative outcomes in accordance with the family.

acceptedSources.summary: 本篇為範疇回顧，目的在整理兒童與青少年使用社群媒體的潛在風險，並提出預防建議。研究依PRISMA指引，以PubMed檢索「social media」或「social network」、「health」與「pediatrics」，排除不相關文獻後納入68篇報告。結果指出，最常被報導的風險包括憂鬱、飲食與心理問題，另也辨識出睡眠、成癮、焦慮、行為問題、身體意象、身體活動、網路誘騙、視力、頭痛與齲齒等相關問題。就本主題而言，摘要僅指出社群媒體使用與睡眠問題可能相關，並提及青少年常使用Instagram、TikTok與YouTube，但未提供針對短影音使用與高中生睡眠品質的專門分析，也未報告效應量、樣本年齡分層或睡眠測量方式，因此對「短影音使用與高中生睡眠品質」的直接證據有限。

acceptedSources.title: Drivers and Consequences of Short-Form Video (SFV) Addiction amongst Adolescents in China: Stress-Coping Theory Perspective
acceptedSources.abstract: As a hedonic technology, short-form videos (SFVs) have attracted numerous users. However, one related problem that merits research is SFV addiction, especially among adolescents due to their immature self-control abilities. Although recent research has discussed the formation process of SFV addiction from psychological needs and the SFV features perspective, scarce attention has been paid to investigating the relationship between stress and SFV addiction, as well as the relationship between SFV addiction and its consequences. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to examine whether school burnout (school stress), social phobia (social stress), and parental phubbing (family stress) trigger SFV addiction based on stress-coping theory and, furthermore, whether SFV addiction leads to low levels of happiness (psychological consequence), parent-child relationship quality (relational consequence), and perseverance (behavioral consequence) among adolescents. The proposed model was tested based on data collected from 242 adolescents from across China under the age of 18 with the experience watching SFVs. A covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) method was used for data analysis. The results showed that school burnout and social phobia significantly triggered SFV addiction, which later negatively and significantly influenced adolescents' happiness, parent-child relationship quality, and perseverance. The study also found that SFV addiction served as a mediator between the drivers and consequences of SFV addiction. This study provides several theoretical implications. First, this study is one of the first to explain adolescents' SFV addiction from stress-coping perspective, thereby enriching research in the field of SFV addiction. Second, prior research has rarely discussed the impacts of stresses from various environments on addiction behavior in a single study. Therefore, this study contributes to the knowledge of stress-related research in an SFV addiction context. Finally, our study enhances our understanding of the impact of SFV addiction on its consequences, in both an SFV research context and a social media research context.

acceptedSources.abstractOriginal: As a hedonic technology, short-form videos (SFVs) have attracted numerous users. However, one related problem that merits research is SFV addiction, especially among adolescents due to their immature self-control abilities. Although recent research has discussed the formation process of SFV addiction from psychological needs and the SFV features perspective, scarce attention has been paid to investigating the relationship between stress and SFV addiction, as well as the relationship between SFV addiction and its consequences. Therefore, this study contributes to the knowledge of stress-related research in an SFV addiction context. Finally, our study enhances our understanding of the impact of SFV addiction on its consequences, in both an SFV research context and a social media research context.

acceptedSources.title: The relationship between short-form video use and depression among Chinese adolescents: Examining the mediating roles of need gratification and short-form video addiction
acceptedSources.abstract: Short-form video apps, such as TikTok, have become popular worldwide. Compared to traditional social media, they have powerful push algorithms and are more entertaining, which might lead to some negative effects. Research has attempted to identify the relationship between short-form video use and depression, but the processes mechanism underly the relationship was few in number. The present study explored the association between short-form video use and depression among Chinese adolescents and analyzed the mediating roles of need gratification and short-form video addiction. The participants included 1302 senior high school students (M age = 16.03, SD = 0.76, 42.6% boys). And a structure equation model with chain mediating was established using Mplus. The results showed (1) a direct association between short-form video use and adolescent depression, (2) that entertainment need gratification, social-related need gratification, and short-form video addiction acted as chain mediating factors, and (3) no gender difference in the model. The present study's findings revealed the important mediating role of addictive behavior between normal use behavior and depression and suggested that preventative and interventional plans based on need gratification should be developed to reduce short-form video addiction and improve mental health.

acceptedSources.title: Social Media Use and Sleep Quality Among Secondary School Students in Aseer Region: A Cross-Sectional Study
acceptedSources.abstract: Background: Use of different social media platforms has increased radically over the past decade, emerging as an important part of adolescents and young people's everyday life. This might exert potential adverse effects on sleep quality and daytime performance of young adults. Aim of Study: To assess the relation between use of social media platforms and sleep quality among public secondary school students. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted on 961 students in Aseer region, Saudi Arabia. Students were asked to fill in a structured interview questionnaire covering personal data, pattern of social media use, sleep quality using The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and their mental health status using the depression, anxiety and stress scale (DASS-21). Results: Students' ages ranged from 15 to 20 years with a mean age of 16.7 ± 2.1 years old. A total of 570 (59.3%) students were females. Tiktok (80%), Snapchat (77.9%), Instagram (63.8%) and YouTube (58.8%) were the most reported platforms used. Regarding their sleep quality, 34.7% of students were poor sleepers. TikTok use (OR 1.33, 95% CI 1.01-1.77), hours spent on social media (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.16-1.37) and having moderate to severe depressive symptoms (OR 1.69, 95% CI 1.19-2.40) were significant independent predictors of poor sleep among the studied sample. Conclusion: The present study emphasized the association between prolonged use of social media and poor sleep quality among Saudi adolescents. Awareness and behavioral change strategies and activities concerning the drawbacks of poor sleep and proper use of social media are urgently called for to control mental and physical health consequences of poor sleep and social media addiction.

acceptedSources.title: The Impact of Short-Form Video Addiction on Sleep Quality: The Mediating Roles of Emotional, Cognitive, and Executive Components
acceptedSources.abstract: With the rapid growth in the number of short-form video users, short-form video addiction (SVA) has drawn increasing attention due to its significant impact on individuals’ daily lives. This study examines the relationship between short-form video addiction and sleep quality, as well as the mediating mechanisms of social anxiety and self-control. Using the College Student Short-Form Video Addiction Scale, the Interaction Anxiousness Scale, the Brief Self-Control Scale, and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, we surveyed 677 Chinese college students. Correlation and mediation analyses were conducted using SPSS and the PROCESS macro. The findings revealed that SVA was negatively associated with sleep quality both directly and indirectly, with higher social anxiety and lower self-control mediating the indirect effect. By showing that addictive behavior is linked to its risk factors through affective, cognitive, and executive pathways, this study provides preliminarily elucidates how addictive behavior feeds back to reinforce its own risk factors proposed in the Interaction of Person–Affect–Cognition–Execution (I-PACE) model.

acceptedSources.title: Adolescents’ short-form video addiction and sleep quality: the mediating role of social anxiety
acceptedSources.abstract: Abstract Background Adolescence is a critical period for individual growth and development. Insufficient sleep adversely affects adolescents’ physical development, blood pressure, vision, and cognitive function. This study examined the effect of short-form video addiction on adolescents’ sleep quality, as well as the mediating role of social anxiety, to identify methods for improving adolescents’ sleep quality in the Internet era. Methods A questionnaire survey was conducted in this cross-sectional study on 1629 adolescents recruited from three high schools. Their short-form video addiction, social anxiety, and sleep quality were evaluated using corresponding scales. Pearson correlation analysis was carried out to analyze the relationships among short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety. Mediating effect analysis was constructed using AMOS 20.0 statistical software. Results Participants’ sleep quality score is 6.12 ± 3.29 points. The detection rate of sleep quality among them is 31.06%. Short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety are significantly correlated ( r = 0.439, 0.404, 0.457, P < 0.001). The direct effect of short-form video addiction on sleep quality is 0.248, accounting for 62.4% of the total effect. The indirect effect exerted through social anxiety is 0.149, accounting for 37.6%. Conclusions Sleep disorders are very common among Chinese adolescents. Short‐form video addiction is positively correlated with adolescents’ sleep quality and social anxiety. Social anxiety partially mediates the relationship between short-form video addiction and sleep quality. The adverse effects of short-form video addiction and social anxiety on the sleep quality of this group must be minimized. Schools are recommended to implement measures to promote sleep quality among adolescents.

acceptedSources.summary: 本研究旨在探討青少年短影音成癮對睡眠品質的影響，並檢驗社交焦慮的中介作用，以尋找網路時代改善睡眠品質的方法。研究採橫斷式問卷調查，納入來自三所高中的1629名青少年，使用相應量表評估短影音成癮、社交焦慮與睡眠品質，並以皮爾森相關與AMOS 20.0進行中介分析。結果顯示，受試者睡眠品質分數為6.12±3.29，睡眠品質異常檢出率為31.06%；短影音成癮、睡眠品質與社交焦慮彼此皆呈顯著相關（r=0.439、0.404、0.457，P<0.001）。短影音成癮對睡眠品質的直接效果為0.248，占總效果62.4%，經由社交焦慮的間接效果為0.149，占37.6%，表示社交焦慮具有部分中介作用。限制在於摘要未提供量表名稱與抽樣細節，且橫斷設計無法推論因果。

acceptedSources.title: The Use of Social Media in Children and Adolescents: Scoping Review on the Potential Risks
acceptedSources.abstract: In recent years, social media has become part of our lives, even among children. From the beginning of COVID-19 pandemic period, media device and Internet access rapidly increased. Adolescents connected Internet alone, consulting social media, mostly Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. During "lockdown", the Internet usage allowed communication with peers and the continuity activities such as school teaching. However, we have to keep in mind that media usage may be related to some adverse consequences especially in the most vulnerable people, such as the young. Aim of the review is to focus on risks correlated to social media use by children and adolescents, identifying spies of rising problems and engaging in preventive recommendations. The scoping review was performed according to PRISMA guidelines, searching on PubMed the terms "social media" or "social network", "health", and "pediatrics". Excluding articles not pertinent, we found 68 reports. Out of them, 19 were dealing with depression, 15 with diet, and 15 with psychological problems, which appeared to be the most reported risk of social media use. Other identified associated problems were sleep, addiction, anxiety, sex related issues, behavioral problems, body image, physical activity, online grooming, sight, headache, and dental caries. Public and medical awareness must rise over this topic and new prevention measures must be found, starting with health practitioners, caregivers, and websites/application developers. Pediatricians should be aware of the risks associated to a problematic social media use for the young's health and identify sentinel signs in children as well as prevent negative outcomes in accordance with the family.

acceptedSources.summary: 本篇為範疇回顧，目的在整理兒童與青少年使用社群媒體的潛在風險，並提出預防建議。研究依PRISMA指引，以PubMed檢索「social media」或「social network」、「health」與「pediatrics」，排除不相關文獻後納入68篇報告。結果指出，最常被報導的風險包括憂鬱、飲食與心理問題，另也辨識出睡眠、成癮、焦慮、行為問題、身體意象、身體活動、網路誘騙、視力、頭痛與齲齒等相關問題。就本主題而言，摘要僅指出社群媒體使用與睡眠問題可能相關，並提及青少年常使用Instagram、TikTok與YouTube，但未提供針對短影音使用與高中生睡眠品質的專門分析，也未報告效應量、樣本年齡分層或睡眠測量方式，因此對「短影音使用與高中生睡眠品質」的直接證據有限。

acceptedSources.title: Drivers and Consequences of Short-Form Video (SFV) Addiction amongst Adolescents in China: Stress-Coping Theory Perspective
acceptedSources.abstract: As a hedonic technology, short-form videos (SFVs) have attracted numerous users. However, one related problem that merits research is SFV addiction, especially among adolescents due to their immature self-control abilities. Although recent research has discussed the formation process of SFV addiction from psychological needs and the SFV features perspective, scarce attention has been paid to investigating the relationship between stress and SFV addiction, as well as the relationship between SFV addiction and its consequences. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to examine whether school burnout (school stress), social phobia (social stress), and parental phubbing (family stress) trigger SFV addiction based on stress-coping theory and, furthermore, whether SFV addiction leads to low levels of happiness (psychological consequence), parent-child relationship quality (relational consequence), and perseverance (behavioral consequence) among adolescents. The proposed model was tested based on data collected from 242 adolescents from across China under the age of 18 with the experience watching SFVs. A covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) method was used for data analysis. The results showed that school burnout and social phobia significantly triggered SFV addiction, which later negatively and significantly influenced adolescents' happiness, parent-child relationship quality, and perseverance. The study also found that SFV addiction served as a mediator between the drivers and consequences of SFV addiction. This study provides several theoretical implications. First, this study is one of the first to explain adolescents' SFV addiction from stress-coping perspective, thereby enriching research in the field of SFV addiction. Second, prior research has rarely discussed the impacts of stresses from various environments on addiction behavior in a single study. Therefore, this study contributes to the knowledge of stress-related research in an SFV addiction context. Finally, our study enhances our understanding of the impact of SFV addiction on its consequences, in both an SFV research context and a social media research context.

acceptedSources.summary: 本研究從壓力因應理論出發，探討中國青少年短影音成癮的驅動因素及其後果。研究以242名中國、未滿18歲且有觀看短影音經驗的青少年為樣本，採共變數基礎結構方程模型分析學校倦怠、社交恐懼與父母低頭行為對短影音成癮的影響，以及成癮對幸福感、親子關係品質與毅力的後果。結果顯示，學校倦怠與社交恐懼會顯著觸發短影音成癮，而短影音成癮進一步顯著降低幸福感、親子關係品質與毅力，且在前因與後果之間具有中介作用。就本題而言，研究有助於理解高中年齡層短影音成癮的心理社會脈絡，但摘要未提供睡眠品質相關測量或結果，因此無法直接支持短影音使用與睡眠品質之關聯；另摘要未提供更細的抽樣來源與量表資訊。

acceptedSources.title: The relationship between short-form video use and depression among Chinese adolescents: Examining the mediating roles of need gratification and short-form video addiction
acceptedSources.abstract: Short-form video apps, such as TikTok, have become popular worldwide. Compared to traditional social media, they have powerful push algorithms and are more entertaining, which might lead to some negative effects. Research has attempted to identify the relationship between short-form video use and depression, but the processes mechanism underly the relationship was few in number. The present study explored the association between short-form video use and depression among Chinese adolescents and analyzed the mediating roles of need gratification and short-form video addiction. The participants included 1302 senior high school students (M age = 16.03, SD = 0.76, 42.6% boys). And a structure equation model with chain mediating was established using Mplus. The results showed (1) a direct association between short-form video use and adolescent depression, (2) that entertainment need gratification, social-related need gratification, and short-form video addiction acted as chain mediating factors, and (3) no gender difference in the model. The present study's findings revealed the important mediating role of addictive behavior between normal use behavior and depression and suggested that preventative and interventional plans based on need gratification should be developed to reduce short-form video addiction and improve mental health.

acceptedSources.title: Social Media Use and Sleep Quality Among Secondary School Students in Aseer Region: A Cross-Sectional Study
acceptedSources.abstract: Background: Use of different social media platforms has increased radically over the past decade, emerging as an important part of adolescents and young people's everyday life. This might exert potential adverse effects on sleep quality and daytime performance of young adults. Aim of Study: To assess the relation between use of social media platforms and sleep quality among public secondary school students. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted on 961 students in Aseer region, Saudi Arabia. Students were asked to fill in a structured interview questionnaire covering personal data, pattern of social media use, sleep quality using The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and their mental health status using the depression, anxiety and stress scale (DASS-21). Results: Students' ages ranged from 15 to 20 years with a mean age of 16.7 ± 2.1 years old. A total of 570 (59.3%) students were females. Tiktok (80%), Snapchat (77.9%), Instagram (63.8%) and YouTube (58.8%) were the most reported platforms used. Regarding their sleep quality, 34.7% of students were poor sleepers. TikTok use (OR 1.33, 95% CI 1.01-1.77), hours spent on social media (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.16-1.37) and having moderate to severe depressive symptoms (OR 1.69, 95% CI 1.19-2.40) were significant independent predictors of poor sleep among the studied sample. Conclusion: The present study emphasized the association between prolonged use of social media and poor sleep quality among Saudi adolescents. Awareness and behavioral change strategies and activities concerning the drawbacks of poor sleep and proper use of social media are urgently called for to control mental and physical health consequences of poor sleep and social media addiction.

acceptedSources.summary: 本研究旨在評估沙烏地阿拉伯Aseer地區公立中學學生社群媒體使用與睡眠品質之關聯。研究採橫斷式設計，納入961名15至20歲學生，以結構式問卷蒐集個人資料、社群媒體使用型態，並以PSQI評估睡眠品質、DASS-21評估心理健康。結果顯示，TikTok為最常使用平台之一（80%），34.7%學生屬睡眠不佳；在多變項分析中，TikTok使用（OR 1.33，95% CI 1.01-1.77）、社群媒體使用時數增加（OR 1.26，95% CI 1.16-1.37）及中重度憂鬱症狀（OR 1.69，95% CI 1.19-2.40）皆為睡眠不佳的獨立預測因子。此研究支持短影音相關平台使用與較差睡眠品質有關，但僅為摘要且屬橫斷研究，無法推論因果，短影音使用細節亦未充分提供。

acceptedSources.title: The Impact of Short-Form Video Addiction on Sleep Quality: The Mediating Roles of Emotional, Cognitive, and Executive Components
acceptedSources.abstract: With the rapid growth in the number of short-form video users, short-form video addiction (SVA) has drawn increasing attention due to its significant impact on individuals’ daily lives. This study examines the relationship between short-form video addiction and sleep quality, as well as the mediating mechanisms of social anxiety and self-control. Using the College Student Short-Form Video Addiction Scale, the Interaction Anxiousness Scale, the Brief Self-Control Scale, and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, we surveyed 677 Chinese college students. Correlation and mediation analyses were conducted using SPSS and the PROCESS macro. The findings revealed that SVA was negatively associated with sleep quality both directly and indirectly, with higher social anxiety and lower self-control mediating the indirect effect. By showing that addictive behavior is linked to its risk factors through affective, cognitive, and executive pathways, this study provides preliminarily elucidates how addictive behavior feeds back to reinforce its own risk factors proposed in the Interaction of Person–Affect–Cognition–Execution (I-PACE) model.

acceptedSources.title: Adolescents’ short-form video addiction and sleep quality: the mediating role of social anxiety
acceptedSources.abstract: Abstract Background Adolescence is a critical period for individual growth and development. Insufficient sleep adversely affects adolescents’ physical development, blood pressure, vision, and cognitive function. This study examined the effect of short-form video addiction on adolescents’ sleep quality, as well as the mediating role of social anxiety, to identify methods for improving adolescents’ sleep quality in the Internet era. Methods A questionnaire survey was conducted in this cross-sectional study on 1629 adolescents recruited from three high schools. Their short-form video addiction, social anxiety, and sleep quality were evaluated using corresponding scales. Pearson correlation analysis was carried out to analyze the relationships among short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety. Mediating effect analysis was constructed using AMOS 20.0 statistical software. Results Participants’ sleep quality score is 6.12 ± 3.29 points. The detection rate of sleep quality among them is 31.06%. Short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety are significantly correlated ( r = 0.439, 0.404, 0.457, P < 0.001). The direct effect of short-form video addiction on sleep quality is 0.248, accounting for 62.4% of the total effect. The indirect effect exerted through social anxiety is 0.149, accounting for 37.6%. Conclusions Sleep disorders are very common among Chinese adolescents. Short‐form video addiction is positively correlated with adolescents’ sleep quality and social anxiety. Social anxiety partially mediates the relationship between short-form video addiction and sleep quality. The adverse effects of short-form video addiction and social anxiety on the sleep quality of this group must be minimized. Schools are recommended to implement measures to promote sleep quality among adolescents.

acceptedSources.summary: 本研究旨在探討青少年短影音成癮對睡眠品質的影響，並檢驗社交焦慮的中介作用，以尋找網路時代改善睡眠品質的方法。研究採橫斷式問卷調查，納入來自三所高中的1629名青少年，使用相應量表評估短影音成癮、社交焦慮與睡眠品質，並以皮爾森相關與AMOS 20.0進行中介分析。結果顯示，受試者睡眠品質分數為6.12±3.29，睡眠品質異常檢出率為31.06%；短影音成癮、睡眠品質與社交焦慮彼此皆呈顯著相關（r=0.439、0.404、0.457，P<0.001）。短影音成癮對睡眠品質的直接效果為0.248，占總效果62.4%，經由社交焦慮的間接效果為0.149，占37.6%，表示社交焦慮具有部分中介作用。限制在於摘要未提供量表名稱與抽樣細節，且橫斷設計無法推論因果。

acceptedSources.title: The Use of Social Media in Children and Adolescents: Scoping Review on the Potential Risks
acceptedSources.abstract: In recent years, social media has become part of our lives, even among children. From the beginning of COVID-19 pandemic period, media device and Internet access rapidly increased. Adolescents connected Internet alone, consulting social media, mostly Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. During "lockdown", the Internet usage allowed communication with peers and the continuity activities such as school teaching. However, we have to keep in mind that media usage may be related to some adverse consequences especially in the most vulnerable people, such as the young. Aim of the review is to focus on risks correlated to social media use by children and adolescents, identifying spies of rising problems and engaging in preventive recommendations. The scoping review was performed according to PRISMA guidelines, searching on PubMed the terms "social media" or "social network", "health", and "pediatrics". Excluding articles not pertinent, we found 68 reports. Out of them, 19 were dealing with depression, 15 with diet, and 15 with psychological problems, which appeared to be the most reported risk of social media use. Other identified associated problems were sleep, addiction, anxiety, sex related issues, behavioral problems, body image, physical activity, online grooming, sight, headache, and dental caries. Public and medical awareness must rise over this topic and new prevention measures must be found, starting with health practitioners, caregivers, and websites/application developers. Pediatricians should be aware of the risks associated to a problematic social media use for the young's health and identify sentinel signs in children as well as prevent negative outcomes in accordance with the family.

acceptedSources.summary: 本篇為範疇回顧，目的在整理兒童與青少年使用社群媒體的潛在風險，並提出預防建議。研究依PRISMA指引，以PubMed檢索「social media」或「social network」、「health」與「pediatrics」，排除不相關文獻後納入68篇報告。結果指出，最常被報導的風險包括憂鬱、飲食與心理問題，另也辨識出睡眠、成癮、焦慮、行為問題、身體意象、身體活動、網路誘騙、視力、頭痛與齲齒等相關問題。就本主題而言，摘要僅指出社群媒體使用與睡眠問題可能相關，並提及青少年常使用Instagram、TikTok與YouTube，但未提供針對短影音使用與高中生睡眠品質的專門分析，也未報告效應量、樣本年齡分層或睡眠測量方式，因此對「短影音使用與高中生睡眠品質」的直接證據有限。

acceptedSources.title: Drivers and Consequences of Short-Form Video (SFV) Addiction amongst Adolescents in China: Stress-Coping Theory Perspective
acceptedSources.abstract: As a hedonic technology, short-form videos (SFVs) have attracted numerous users. However, one related problem that merits research is SFV addiction, especially among adolescents due to their immature self-control abilities. Although recent research has discussed the formation process of SFV addiction from psychological needs and the SFV features perspective, scarce attention has been paid to investigating the relationship between stress and SFV addiction, as well as the relationship between SFV addiction and its consequences. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to examine whether school burnout (school stress), social phobia (social stress), and parental phubbing (family stress) trigger SFV addiction based on stress-coping theory and, furthermore, whether SFV addiction leads to low levels of happiness (psychological consequence), parent-child relationship quality (relational consequence), and perseverance (behavioral consequence) among adolescents. The proposed model was tested based on data collected from 242 adolescents from across China under the age of 18 with the experience watching SFVs. A covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) method was used for data analysis. The results showed that school burnout and social phobia significantly triggered SFV addiction, which later negatively and significantly influenced adolescents' happiness, parent-child relationship quality, and perseverance. The study also found that SFV addiction served as a mediator between the drivers and consequences of SFV addiction. This study provides several theoretical implications. First, this study is one of the first to explain adolescents' SFV addiction from stress-coping perspective, thereby enriching research in the field of SFV addiction. Second, prior research has rarely discussed the impacts of stresses from various environments on addiction behavior in a single study. Therefore, this study contributes to the knowledge of stress-related research in an SFV addiction context. Finally, our study enhances our understanding of the impact of SFV addiction on its consequences, in both an SFV research context and a social media research context.

acceptedSources.summary: 本研究從壓力因應理論出發，探討中國青少年短影音成癮的驅動因素及其後果。研究以242名中國、未滿18歲且有觀看短影音經驗的青少年為樣本，採共變數基礎結構方程模型分析學校倦怠、社交恐懼與父母低頭行為對短影音成癮的影響，以及成癮對幸福感、親子關係品質與毅力的後果。結果顯示，學校倦怠與社交恐懼會顯著觸發短影音成癮，而短影音成癮進一步顯著降低幸福感、親子關係品質與毅力，且在前因與後果之間具有中介作用。就本題而言，研究有助於理解高中年齡層短影音成癮的心理社會脈絡，但摘要未提供睡眠品質相關測量或結果，因此無法直接支持短影音使用與睡眠品質之關聯；另摘要未提供更細的抽樣來源與量表資訊。

acceptedSources.title: The relationship between short-form video use and depression among Chinese adolescents: Examining the mediating roles of need gratification and short-form video addiction
acceptedSources.abstract: Short-form video apps, such as TikTok, have become popular worldwide. Compared to traditional social media, they have powerful push algorithms and are more entertaining, which might lead to some negative effects. Research has attempted to identify the relationship between short-form video use and depression, but the processes mechanism underly the relationship was few in number. The present study explored the association between short-form video use and depression among Chinese adolescents and analyzed the mediating roles of need gratification and short-form video addiction. The participants included 1302 senior high school students (M age = 16.03, SD = 0.76, 42.6% boys). And a structure equation model with chain mediating was established using Mplus. The results showed (1) a direct association between short-form video use and adolescent depression, (2) that entertainment need gratification, social-related need gratification, and short-form video addiction acted as chain mediating factors, and (3) no gender difference in the model. The present study's findings revealed the important mediating role of addictive behavior between normal use behavior and depression and suggested that preventative and interventional plans based on need gratification should be developed to reduce short-form video addiction and improve mental health.

acceptedSources.title: Social Media Use and Sleep Quality Among Secondary School Students in Aseer Region: A Cross-Sectional Study
acceptedSources.abstract: Background: Use of different social media platforms has increased radically over the past decade, emerging as an important part of adolescents and young people's everyday life. This might exert potential adverse effects on sleep quality and daytime performance of young adults. Aim of Study: To assess the relation between use of social media platforms and sleep quality among public secondary school students. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted on 961 students in Aseer region, Saudi Arabia. Students were asked to fill in a structured interview questionnaire covering personal data, pattern of social media use, sleep quality using The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and their mental health status using the depression, anxiety and stress scale (DASS-21). Results: Students' ages ranged from 15 to 20 years with a mean age of 16.7 ± 2.1 years old. A total of 570 (59.3%) students were females. Tiktok (80%), Snapchat (77.9%), Instagram (63.8%) and YouTube (58.8%) were the most reported platforms used. Regarding their sleep quality, 34.7% of students were poor sleepers. TikTok use (OR 1.33, 95% CI 1.01-1.77), hours spent on social media (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.16-1.37) and having moderate to severe depressive symptoms (OR 1.69, 95% CI 1.19-2.40) were significant independent predictors of poor sleep among the studied sample. Conclusion: The present study emphasized the association between prolonged use of social media and poor sleep quality among Saudi adolescents. Awareness and behavioral change strategies and activities concerning the drawbacks of poor sleep and proper use of social media are urgently called for to control mental and physical health consequences of poor sleep and social media addiction.

acceptedSources.summary: 本研究旨在評估沙烏地阿拉伯Aseer地區公立中學學生社群媒體使用與睡眠品質之關聯。研究採橫斷式設計，納入961名15至20歲學生，以結構式問卷蒐集個人資料、社群媒體使用型態，並以PSQI評估睡眠品質、DASS-21評估心理健康。結果顯示，TikTok為最常使用平台之一（80%），34.7%學生屬睡眠不佳；在多變項分析中，TikTok使用（OR 1.33，95% CI 1.01-1.77）、社群媒體使用時數增加（OR 1.26，95% CI 1.16-1.37）及中重度憂鬱症狀（OR 1.69，95% CI 1.19-2.40）皆為睡眠不佳的獨立預測因子。此研究支持短影音相關平台使用與較差睡眠品質有關，但僅為摘要且屬橫斷研究，無法推論因果，短影音使用細節亦未充分提供。

acceptedSources.title: The Impact of Short-Form Video Addiction on Sleep Quality: The Mediating Roles of Emotional, Cognitive, and Executive Components
acceptedSources.abstract: With the rapid growth in the number of short-form video users, short-form video addiction (SVA) has drawn increasing attention due to its significant impact on individuals’ daily lives. This study examines the relationship between short-form video addiction and sleep quality, as well as the mediating mechanisms of social anxiety and self-control. Using the College Student Short-Form Video Addiction Scale, the Interaction Anxiousness Scale, the Brief Self-Control Scale, and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, we surveyed 677 Chinese college students. Correlation and mediation analyses were conducted using SPSS and the PROCESS macro. The findings revealed that SVA was negatively associated with sleep quality both directly and indirectly, with higher social anxiety and lower self-control mediating the indirect effect. By showing that addictive behavior is linked to its risk factors through affective, cognitive, and executive pathways, this study provides preliminarily elucidates how addictive behavior feeds back to reinforce its own risk factors proposed in the Interaction of Person–Affect–Cognition–Execution (I-PACE) model.

acceptedSources.summary: 本研究探討短影音成癮與睡眠品質之關係，並檢驗社交焦慮與自我控制的中介作用。研究對677名中國大學生進行問卷調查，使用短影音成癮量表、互動焦慮量表、簡式自我控制量表與PSQI，並以相關分析及中介分析處理資料。結果指出，短影音成癮與睡眠品質呈負向關聯，亦即成癮程度越高，睡眠品質越差；此外，較高社交焦慮與較低自我控制會中介此間接效果。研究並以I-PACE模型說明情緒、認知與執行功能路徑可能如何連結成癮行為與睡眠問題。惟樣本為大學生而非高中生，摘要未提供更細部效應值，且研究設計無法確認因果方向。

evidenceCards.title: Adolescents’ short-form video addiction and sleep quality: the mediating role of social anxiety
evidenceCards.claim: 本研究旨在探討青少年短影音成癮對睡眠品質的影響，並檢驗社交焦慮的中介作用，以尋找網路時代改善睡眠品質的方法。研究採橫斷式問卷調查，納入來自三所高中的1629名青少年，使用相應量表評估短影音成癮、社交焦慮與睡眠品質，並以皮爾森相關與AMOS 20.0進行中介分析。結果顯示，受試者睡眠品質分數為6.12±3.29，睡眠品質異常檢出率為31.06%；短影音成癮、睡眠品質與社交焦慮彼此皆呈顯著相關（r=0.439、0.404、0.457，P<0.001）。短影音成癮對睡眠品質的直接效果為0.248，占總效果62.4%，經由社交焦慮的間接效果為0.149，占37.6%，表示社交焦慮具有部分中介作用。限制在於摘要未提供量表名稱與抽樣細節，且橫斷設計無法推論因果。

evidenceCards.supportSpan: Abstract Background Adolescence is a critical period for individual growth and development. Insufficient sleep adversely affects adolescents’ physical development, blood pressure, vision, and cognitive function. This study examined the effect of short-form video addiction on adolescents’ sleep quality, as well as the mediating role of social anxiety, to identify methods for improving adolescents’ sleep quality in the Internet era. Methods A questionnaire survey was conducted in this cross-sectional study on 1629 adolescents recruited from three high schools. Their short-form video addiction, social anxiety, and sleep quality were evaluated using corresponding scales. Pearson correlation analysis was carried out to analyze the relationships among short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety. Mediating effect analysis was constructed using AMOS 20.0 statistical software. Results Participants’ sleep quality score is 6.12 ± 3.29 points. The detection rate of sleep quality among them is 31.06%. Short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety are significantly correlated ( r = 0.439, 0.404, 0.457, P < 0.001). The direct effect of short-form video addiction on sleep quality is 0.248, accounting for 62.4% of the total effect. The indirect effect exerted through social anxiety is 0.149, accounting for 37.6%. Conclusions Sleep disorders are very common among Chinese adolescents. Short‐form video addiction is positively correlated with adolescents’ sleep quality and social anxiety. Social anxiety partially mediates the relationship between short-form video addiction and sleep quality. The adverse effects of short-form video addiction and social anxiety on the sleep quality of this group must be minimized. Schools are recommended to implement measures to promote sleep quality among adolescents.

evidenceCards.title: The Use of Social Media in Children and Adolescents: Scoping Review on the Potential Risks
evidenceCards.claim: 本篇為範疇回顧，目的在整理兒童與青少年使用社群媒體的潛在風險，並提出預防建議。研究依PRISMA指引，以PubMed檢索「social media」或「social network」、「health」與「pediatrics」，排除不相關文獻後納入68篇報告。結果指出，最常被報導的風險包括憂鬱、飲食與心理問題，另也辨識出睡眠、成癮、焦慮、行為問題、身體意象、身體活動、網路誘騙、視力、頭痛與齲齒等相關問題。就本主題而言，摘要僅指出社群媒體使用與睡眠問題可能相關，並提及青少年常使用Instagram、TikTok與YouTube，但未提供針對短影音使用與高中生睡眠品質的專門分析，也未報告效應量、樣本年齡分層或睡眠測量方式，因此對「短影音使用與高中生睡眠品質」的直接證據有限。

evidenceCards.supportSpan: In recent years, social media has become part of our lives, even among children. From the beginning of COVID-19 pandemic period, media device and Internet access rapidly increased. Adolescents connected Internet alone, consulting social media, mostly Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. During "lockdown", the Internet usage allowed communication with peers and the continuity activities such as school teaching. However, we have to keep in mind that media usage may be related to some adverse consequences especially in the most vulnerable people, such as the young. Aim of the review is to focus on risks correlated to social media use by children and adolescents, identifying spies of rising problems and engaging in preventive recommendations. The scoping review was performed according to PRISMA guidelines, searching on PubMed the terms "social media" or "social network", "health", and "pediatrics". Excluding articles not pertinent, we found 68 reports. Out of them, 19 were dealing with depression, 15 with diet, and 15 with psychological problems, which appeared to be the most reported risk of social media use. Other identified associated problems were sleep, addiction, anxiety, sex related issues, behavioral problems, body image, physical activity, online grooming, sight, headache, and dental caries. Public and medical awareness must rise over this topic and new prevention measures must be found, starting with health practitioners, caregivers, and websites/application developers. Pediatricians should be aware of the risks associated to a problematic social media use for the young's health and identify sentinel signs in children as well as prevent negative outcomes in accordance with the family.

evidenceCards.sourceTitle: The Use of Social Media in Children and Adolescents: Scoping Review on the Potential Risks
evidenceCards.venue: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
evidenceCards.abstract: In recent years, social media has become part of our lives, even among children. From the beginning of COVID-19 pandemic period, media device and Internet access rapidly increased. Adolescents connected Internet alone, consulting social media, mostly Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. During "lockdown", the Internet usage allowed communication with peers and the continuity activities such as school teaching. However, we have to keep in mind that media usage may be related to some adverse consequences especially in the most vulnerable people, such as the young. Aim of the review is to focus on risks correlated to social media use by children and adolescents, identifying spies of rising problems and engaging in preventive recommendations. The scoping review was performed according to PRISMA guidelines, searching on PubMed the terms "social media" or "social network", "health", and "pediatrics". Excluding articles not pertinent, we found 68 reports. Out of them, 19 were dealing with depression, 15 with diet, and 15 with psychological problems, which appeared to be the most reported risk of social media use. Other identified associated problems were sleep, addiction, anxiety, sex related issues, behavioral problems, body image, physical activity, online grooming, sight, headache, and dental caries. Public and medical awareness must rise over this topic and new prevention measures must be found, starting with health practitioners, caregivers, and websites/application developers. Pediatricians should be aware of the risks associated to a problematic social media use for the young's health and identify sentinel signs in children as well as prevent negative outcomes in accordance with the family.

evidenceCards.title: Drivers and Consequences of Short-Form Video (SFV) Addiction amongst Adolescents in China: Stress-Coping Theory Perspective
evidenceCards.claim: 本研究從壓力因應理論出發，探討中國青少年短影音成癮的驅動因素及其後果。研究以242名中國、未滿18歲且有觀看短影音經驗的青少年為樣本，採共變數基礎結構方程模型分析學校倦怠、社交恐懼與父母低頭行為對短影音成癮的影響，以及成癮對幸福感、親子關係品質與毅力的後果。結果顯示，學校倦怠與社交恐懼會顯著觸發短影音成癮，而短影音成癮進一步顯著降低幸福感、親子關係品質與毅力，且在前因與後果之間具有中介作用。就本題而言，研究有助於理解高中年齡層短影音成癮的心理社會脈絡，但摘要未提供睡眠品質相關測量或結果，因此無法直接支持短影音使用與睡眠品質之關聯；另摘要未提供更細的抽樣來源與量表資訊。

evidenceCards.supportSpan: As a hedonic technology, short-form videos (SFVs) have attracted numerous users. However, one related problem that merits research is SFV addiction, especially among adolescents due to their immature self-control abilities. Although recent research has discussed the formation process of SFV addiction from psychological needs and the SFV features perspective, scarce attention has been paid to investigating the relationship between stress and SFV addiction, as well as the relationship between SFV addiction and its consequences. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to examine whether school burnout (school stress), social phobia (social stress), and parental phubbing (family stress) trigger SFV addiction based on stress-coping theory and, furthermore, whether SFV addiction leads to low levels of happiness (psychological consequence), parent-child relationship quality (relational consequence), and perseverance (behavioral consequence) among adolescents. The proposed model was tested based on data collected from 242 adolescents from across China under the age of 18 with the experience watching SFVs. A covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) method was used for data analysis. The results showed that school burnout and social phobia significantly triggered SFV addiction, which later negatively and significantly influenced adolescents' happiness, parent-child relationship quality, and perseverance. The study also found that SFV addiction served as a mediator between the drivers and consequences of SFV addiction. This study provides several theoretical implications. First, this study is one of the first to explain adolescents' SFV addiction from stress-coping perspective, thereby enriching research in the field of SFV addiction. Second, prior research has rarely discussed the impacts of stresses from various environments on addiction behavior in a single study. Therefore, this study contributes to the knowledge of stress-related research in an SFV addiction context. Finally, our study enhances our understanding of the impact of SFV addiction on its consequences, in both an SFV research context and a social media research context.

evidenceCards.title: The relationship between short-form video use and depression among Chinese adolescents: Examining the mediating roles of need gratification and short-form video addiction
evidenceCards.claim: 本研究旨在探討中國青少年短影音使用與憂鬱之間的關係，並檢驗需求滿足與短影音成癮的中介作用。樣本為1302名高中生，平均年齡16.03歲（SD=0.76），其中42.6%為男生；研究以Mplus建立鏈式中介的結構方程模型。結果顯示，短影音使用與青少年憂鬱存在直接關聯，娛樂需求滿足、社交相關需求滿足與短影音成癮可作為鏈式中介因素，且模型未見性別差異。研究指出，從一般使用行為到心理健康結果之間，成癮行為扮演重要中介角色，並建議依需求滿足發展預防與介入方案。限制在於摘要未提供睡眠品質資料，因此對「短影音使用與高中生睡眠品質」僅具間接參考價值，且未說明量表名稱與抽樣程序。

evidenceCards.supportSpan: Short-form video apps, such as TikTok, have become popular worldwide. Compared to traditional social media, they have powerful push algorithms and are more entertaining, which might lead to some negative effects. Research has attempted to identify the relationship between short-form video use and depression, but the processes mechanism underly the relationship was few in number. The present study explored the association between short-form video use and depression among Chinese adolescents and analyzed the mediating roles of need gratification and short-form video addiction. The participants included 1302 senior high school students (M age = 16.03, SD = 0.76, 42.6% boys). And a structure equation model with chain mediating was established using Mplus. The results showed (1) a direct association between short-form video use and adolescent depression, (2) that entertainment need gratification, social-related need gratification, and short-form video addiction acted as chain mediating factors, and (3) no gender difference in the model. The present study's findings revealed the important mediating role of addictive behavior between normal use behavior and depression and suggested that preventative and interventional plans based on need gratification should be developed to reduce short-form video addiction and improve mental health.

evidenceCards.title: Social Media Use and Sleep Quality Among Secondary School Students in Aseer Region: A Cross-Sectional Study
evidenceCards.claim: 本研究旨在評估沙烏地阿拉伯Aseer地區公立中學學生社群媒體使用與睡眠品質之關聯。研究採橫斷式設計，納入961名15至20歲學生，以結構式問卷蒐集個人資料、社群媒體使用型態，並以PSQI評估睡眠品質、DASS-21評估心理健康。結果顯示，TikTok為最常使用平台之一（80%），34.7%學生屬睡眠不佳；在多變項分析中，TikTok使用（OR 1.33，95% CI 1.01-1.77）、社群媒體使用時數增加（OR 1.26，95% CI 1.16-1.37）及中重度憂鬱症狀（OR 1.69，95% CI 1.19-2.40）皆為睡眠不佳的獨立預測因子。此研究支持短影音相關平台使用與較差睡眠品質有關，但僅為摘要且屬橫斷研究，無法推論因果，短影音使用細節亦未充分提供。

evidenceCards.supportSpan: Background: Use of different social media platforms has increased radically over the past decade, emerging as an important part of adolescents and young people's everyday life. This might exert potential adverse effects on sleep quality and daytime performance of young adults. Aim of Study: To assess the relation between use of social media platforms and sleep quality among public secondary school students. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted on 961 students in Aseer region, Saudi Arabia. Students were asked to fill in a structured interview questionnaire covering personal data, pattern of social media use, sleep quality using The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and their mental health status using the depression, anxiety and stress scale (DASS-21). Results: Students' ages ranged from 15 to 20 years with a mean age of 16.7 ± 2.1 years old. A total of 570 (59.3%) students were females. Tiktok (80%), Snapchat (77.9%), Instagram (63.8%) and YouTube (58.8%) were the most reported platforms used. Regarding their sleep quality, 34.7% of students were poor sleepers. TikTok use (OR 1.33, 95% CI 1.01-1.77), hours spent on social media (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.16-1.37) and having moderate to severe depressive symptoms (OR 1.69, 95% CI 1.19-2.40) were significant independent predictors of poor sleep among the studied sample. Conclusion: The present study emphasized the association between prolonged use of social media and poor sleep quality among Saudi adolescents. Awareness and behavioral change strategies and activities concerning the drawbacks of poor sleep and proper use of social media are urgently called for to control mental and physical health consequences of poor sleep and social media addiction.

evidenceCards.claim: 本研究探討短影音成癮與睡眠品質之關係，並檢驗社交焦慮與自我控制的中介作用。研究對677名中國大學生進行問卷調查，使用短影音成癮量表、互動焦慮量表、簡式自我控制量表與PSQI，並以相關分析及中介分析處理資料。結果指出，短影音成癮與睡眠品質呈負向關聯，亦即成癮程度越高，睡眠品質越差；此外，較高社交焦慮與較低自我控制會中介此間接效果。研究並以I-PACE模型說明情緒、認知與執行功能路徑可能如何連結成癮行為與睡眠問題。惟樣本為大學生而非高中生，摘要未提供更細部效應值，且研究設計無法確認因果方向。

evidenceCards.supportSpan: With the rapid growth in the number of short-form video users, short-form video addiction (SVA) has drawn increasing attention due to its significant impact on individuals’ daily lives. This study examines the relationship between short-form video addiction and sleep quality, as well as the mediating mechanisms of social anxiety and self-control. Using the College Student Short-Form Video Addiction Scale, the Interaction Anxiousness Scale, the Brief Self-Control Scale, and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, we surveyed 677 Chinese college students. Correlation and mediation analyses were conducted using SPSS and the PROCESS macro. The findings revealed that SVA was negatively associated with sleep quality both directly and indirectly, with higher social anxiety and lower self-control mediating the indirect effect. By showing that addictive behavior is linked to its risk factors through affective, cognitive, and executive pathways, this study provides preliminarily elucidates how addictive behavior feeds back to reinforce its own risk factors proposed in the Interaction of Person–Affect–Cognition–Execution (I-PACE) model.

sections.goal: 回答子問題：關於「Short-form video use and sleep quality among high school students」，主要結果能支持什麼判斷？；關於「Short-form video use and sleep quality among high school students」，共同研究方法的證據能支持什麼判斷？；關於「Short-form video use and sleep quality among high school students」，研究方法與數值可比較性能支持什麼判斷？

sections.sectionClaim: cross-sectional、Cross-Sectional、人本觀測回答的是不同層次的問題；研究數值只有在暴露、結果、單位與比較基準相容時才可合併。；主要結果在多個獨立來源中形成可比較的方向性證據，但效果量只可在量測定義相容時比較。；本研究旨在探討青少年短影音成癮對睡眠品質的影響，並檢驗社交焦慮的中介作用，以尋找網路時代改善睡眠品質的方法。研究採橫斷式問卷調查，納入來自三所高中的1629名青少年，使用相應量表評估短影音成癮、社交焦慮與睡眠品質，並以皮爾森相關與AMOS 20.0進行中介分析。結果顯示，受試者睡眠品質分數為6.12±3.29，睡眠品質異常檢出率為31.06%；短影音成癮、睡眠品質與社交焦慮彼此皆呈顯著相關（r=0.439、0.404、0.457，P<0.001）。短影音成癮對睡眠品質的直接效果為0.248，占總效果62.4%，經由社交焦慮的間接效果為0.149，占37.6%，表示社交焦慮具有部分中介作用。限制在於摘要未提供量表名稱與抽樣細節，且橫斷設計無法推論因果。

evidenceGroups.label: 主要結果與共同研究場域的證據與共同研究方法的證據與研究方法與數值可比較性
evidenceGroups.sharedFinding: cross-sectional、Cross-Sectional、人本觀測回答的是不同層次的問題；研究數值只有在暴露、結果、單位與比較基準相容時才可合併。；主要結果在多個獨立來源中形成可比較的方向性證據，但效果量只可在量測定義相容時比較。；共同研究場域的證據的跨來源結果方向不完全一致，須依研究場域、方法與量測指標分別解讀。；本研究旨在探討青少年短影音成癮對睡眠品質的影響，並檢驗社交焦慮的中介作用，以尋找網路時代改善睡眠品質的方法。研究採橫斷式問卷調查，納入來自三所高中的1629名青少年，使用相應量表評估短影音成癮、社交焦慮與睡眠品質，並以皮爾森相關與AMOS 20.0進行中介分析。結果顯示，受試者睡眠品質分數為6.12±3.29，睡眠品質異常檢出率為31.06%；短影音成癮、睡眠品質與社交焦慮彼此皆呈顯著相關（r=0.439、0.404、0.457，P<0.001）。短影音成癮對睡眠品質的直接效果為0.248，占總效果62.4%，經由社交焦慮的間接效果為0.149，占37.6%，表示社交焦慮具有部分中介作用。限制在於摘要未提供量表名稱與抽樣細節，且橫斷設計無法推論因果。

evidenceGroups.label: 主要結果與共同研究場域的證據與共同研究方法的證據與研究方法與數值可比較性
evidenceGroups.sharedFinding: cross-sectional、Cross-Sectional、人本觀測回答的是不同層次的問題；研究數值只有在暴露、結果、單位與比較基準相容時才可合併。；主要結果在多個獨立來源中形成可比較的方向性證據，但效果量只可在量測定義相容時比較。；共同研究場域的證據的跨來源結果方向不完全一致，須依研究場域、方法與量測指標分別解讀。；本研究旨在探討青少年短影音成癮對睡眠品質的影響，並檢驗社交焦慮的中介作用，以尋找網路時代改善睡眠品質的方法。研究採橫斷式問卷調查，納入來自三所高中的1629名青少年，使用相應量表評估短影音成癮、社交焦慮與睡眠品質，並以皮爾森相關與AMOS 20.0進行中介分析。結果顯示，受試者睡眠品質分數為6.12±3.29，睡眠品質異常檢出率為31.06%；短影音成癮、睡眠品質與社交焦慮彼此皆呈顯著相關（r=0.439、0.404、0.457，P<0.001）。短影音成癮對睡眠品質的直接效果為0.248，占總效果62.4%，經由社交焦慮的間接效果為0.149，占37.6%，表示社交焦慮具有部分中介作用。限制在於摘要未提供量表名稱與抽樣細節，且橫斷設計無法推論因果。

evidenceGroups.label: 主要結果與共同研究場域的證據與共同研究方法的證據與研究方法與數值可比較性
evidenceGroups.sharedFinding: cross-sectional、Cross-Sectional、人本觀測回答的是不同層次的問題；研究數值只有在暴露、結果、單位與比較基準相容時才可合併。；主要結果在多個獨立來源中形成可比較的方向性證據，但效果量只可在量測定義相容時比較。；共同研究場域的證據的跨來源結果方向不完全一致，須依研究場域、方法與量測指標分別解讀。；本研究旨在探討青少年短影音成癮對睡眠品質的影響，並檢驗社交焦慮的中介作用，以尋找網路時代改善睡眠品質的方法。研究採橫斷式問卷調查，納入來自三所高中的1629名青少年，使用相應量表評估短影音成癮、社交焦慮與睡眠品質，並以皮爾森相關與AMOS 20.0進行中介分析。結果顯示，受試者睡眠品質分數為6.12±3.29，睡眠品質異常檢出率為31.06%；短影音成癮、睡眠品質與社交焦慮彼此皆呈顯著相關（r=0.439、0.404、0.457，P<0.001）。短影音成癮對睡眠品質的直接效果為0.248，占總效果62.4%，經由社交焦慮的間接效果為0.149，占37.6%，表示社交焦慮具有部分中介作用。限制在於摘要未提供量表名稱與抽樣細節，且橫斷設計無法推論因果。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Short-form video apps, such as TikTok, have become popular worldwide. Compared to traditional social media, they have powerful push algorithms and are more entertaining, which might lead to some negative effects. Research has attempted to identify the relationship between short-form video use and depression, but the processes mechanism underly the relationship was few in number. The present study explored the association between short-form video use and depression among Chinese adolescents and analyzed the mediating roles of need gratification and short-form video addiction. The participants included 1302 senior high school students (M age = 16.03, SD = 0.76, 42.6% boys). And a structure equation model with chain mediating was established using Mplus. The results showed (1) a direct association between short-form video use and adolescent depression, (2) that entertainment need gratification, social-related need gratification, and short-form video addiction acted as chain mediating factors, and (3) no gender difference in the model. The present study's findings revealed the important mediating role of addictive behavior between normal use behavior and depression and suggested that preventative and interventional plans based on need gratification should be developed to reduce short-form video addiction and improve mental health.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 本研究旨在探討中國青少年短影音使用與憂鬱之間的關係，並檢驗需求滿足與短影音成癮的中介作用。樣本為1302名高中生，平均年齡16.03歲（SD=0.76），其中42.6%為男生；研究以Mplus建立鏈式中介的結構方程模型。結果顯示，短影音使用與青少年憂鬱存在直接關聯，娛樂需求滿足、社交相關需求滿足與短影音成癮可作為鏈式中介因素，且模型未見性別差異。研究指出，從一般使用行為到心理健康結果之間，成癮行為扮演重要中介角色，並建議依需求滿足發展預防與介入方案。限制在於摘要未提供睡眠品質資料，因此對「短影音使用與高中生睡眠品質」僅具間接參考價值，且未說明量表名稱與抽樣程序。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Abstract Background Adolescence is a critical period for individual growth and development. Insufficient sleep adversely affects adolescents’ physical development, blood pressure, vision, and cognitive function. This study examined the effect of short-form video addiction on adolescents’ sleep quality, as well as the mediating role of social anxiety, to identify methods for improving adolescents’ sleep quality in the Internet era. Methods A questionnaire survey was conducted in this cross-sectional study on 1629 adolescents recruited from three high schools. Their short-form video addiction, social anxiety, and sleep quality were evaluated using corresponding scales. Pearson correlation analysis was carried out to analyze the relationships among short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety. Mediating effect analysis was constructed using AMOS 20.0 statistical software. Results Participants’ sleep quality score is 6.12 ± 3.29 points. The detection rate of sleep quality among them is 31.06%. Short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety are significantly correlated ( r = 0.439, 0.404, 0.457, P < 0.001). The direct effect of short-form video addiction on sleep quality is 0.248, accounting for 62.4% of the total effect. The indirect effect exerted through social anxiety is 0.149, accounting for 37.6%. Conclusions Sleep disorders are very common among Chinese adolescents. Short‐form video addiction is positively correlated with adolescents’ sleep quality and social anxiety. Social anxiety partially mediates the relationship between short-form video addiction and sleep quality. The adverse effects of short-form video addiction and social anxiety on the sleep quality of this group must be minimized. Schools are recommended to implement measures to promote sleep quality among adolescents.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 本研究旨在探討青少年短影音成癮對睡眠品質的影響，並檢驗社交焦慮的中介作用，以尋找網路時代改善睡眠品質的方法。研究採橫斷式問卷調查，納入來自三所高中的1629名青少年，使用相應量表評估短影音成癮、社交焦慮與睡眠品質，並以皮爾森相關與AMOS 20.0進行中介分析。結果顯示，受試者睡眠品質分數為6.12±3.29，睡眠品質異常檢出率為31.06%；短影音成癮、睡眠品質與社交焦慮彼此皆呈顯著相關（r=0.439、0.404、0.457，P<0.001）。短影音成癮對睡眠品質的直接效果為0.248，占總效果62.4%，經由社交焦慮的間接效果為0.149，占37.6%，表示社交焦慮具有部分中介作用。限制在於摘要未提供量表名稱與抽樣細節，且橫斷設計無法推論因果。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Background: Use of different social media platforms has increased radically over the past decade, emerging as an important part of adolescents and young people's everyday life. This might exert potential adverse effects on sleep quality and daytime performance of young adults. Aim of Study: To assess the relation between use of social media platforms and sleep quality among public secondary school students. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted on 961 students in Aseer region, Saudi Arabia. Students were asked to fill in a structured interview questionnaire covering personal data, pattern of social media use, sleep quality using The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and their mental health status using the depression, anxiety and stress scale (DASS-21). Results: Students' ages ranged from 15 to 20 years with a mean age of 16.7 ± 2.1 years old. A total of 570 (59.3%) students were females. Tiktok (80%), Snapchat (77.9%), Instagram (63.8%) and YouTube (58.8%) were the most reported platforms used. Regarding their sleep quality, 34.7% of students were poor sleepers. TikTok use (OR 1.33, 95% CI 1.01-1.77), hours spent on social media (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.16-1.37) and having moderate to severe depressive symptoms (OR 1.69, 95% CI 1.19-2.40) were significant independent predictors of poor sleep among the studied sample. Conclusion: The present study emphasized the association between prolonged use of social media and poor sleep quality among Saudi adolescents. Awareness and behavioral change strategies and activities concerning the drawbacks of poor sleep and proper use of social media are urgently called for to control mental and physical health consequences of poor sleep and social media addiction.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 本研究旨在評估沙烏地阿拉伯Aseer地區公立中學學生社群媒體使用與睡眠品質之關聯。研究採橫斷式設計，納入961名15至20歲學生，以結構式問卷蒐集個人資料、社群媒體使用型態，並以PSQI評估睡眠品質、DASS-21評估心理健康。結果顯示，TikTok為最常使用平台之一（80%），34.7%學生屬睡眠不佳；在多變項分析中，TikTok使用（OR 1.33，95% CI 1.01-1.77）、社群媒體使用時數增加（OR 1.26，95% CI 1.16-1.37）及中重度憂鬱症狀（OR 1.69，95% CI 1.19-2.40）皆為睡眠不佳的獨立預測因子。此研究支持短影音相關平台使用與較差睡眠品質有關，但僅為摘要且屬橫斷研究，無法推論因果，短影音使用細節亦未充分提供。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: With the rapid growth in the number of short-form video users, short-form video addiction (SVA) has drawn increasing attention due to its significant impact on individuals’ daily lives. This study examines the relationship between short-form video addiction and sleep quality, as well as the mediating mechanisms of social anxiety and self-control. Using the College Student Short-Form Video Addiction Scale, the Interaction Anxiousness Scale, the Brief Self-Control Scale, and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, we surveyed 677 Chinese college students. Correlation and mediation analyses were conducted using SPSS and the PROCESS macro. The findings revealed that SVA was negatively associated with sleep quality both directly and indirectly, with higher social anxiety and lower self-control mediating the indirect effect. By showing that addictive behavior is linked to its risk factors through affective, cognitive, and executive pathways, this study provides preliminarily elucidates how addictive behavior feeds back to reinforce its own risk factors proposed in the Interaction of Person–Affect–Cognition–Execution (I-PACE) model.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 本研究探討短影音成癮與睡眠品質之關係，並檢驗社交焦慮與自我控制的中介作用。研究對677名中國大學生進行問卷調查，使用短影音成癮量表、互動焦慮量表、簡式自我控制量表與PSQI，並以相關分析及中介分析處理資料。結果指出，短影音成癮與睡眠品質呈負向關聯，亦即成癮程度越高，睡眠品質越差；此外，較高社交焦慮與較低自我控制會中介此間接效果。研究並以I-PACE模型說明情緒、認知與執行功能路徑可能如何連結成癮行為與睡眠問題。惟樣本為大學生而非高中生，摘要未提供更細部效應值，且研究設計無法確認因果方向。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: In recent years, social media has become part of our lives, even among children. From the beginning of COVID-19 pandemic period, media device and Internet access rapidly increased. Adolescents connected Internet alone, consulting social media, mostly Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. During "lockdown", the Internet usage allowed communication with peers and the continuity activities such as school teaching. However, we have to keep in mind that media usage may be related to some adverse consequences especially in the most vulnerable people, such as the young. Aim of the review is to focus on risks correlated to social media use by children and adolescents, identifying spies of rising problems and engaging in preventive recommendations. The scoping review was performed according to PRISMA guidelines, searching on PubMed the terms "social media" or "social network", "health", and "pediatrics". Excluding articles not pertinent, we found 68 reports. Out of them, 19 were dealing with depression, 15 with diet, and 15 with psychological problems, which appeared to be the most reported risk of social media use. Other identified associated problems were sleep, addiction, anxiety, sex related issues, behavioral problems, body image, physical activity, online grooming, sight, headache, and dental caries. Public and medical awareness must rise over this topic and new prevention measures must be found, starting with health practitioners, caregivers, and websites/application developers. Pediatricians should be aware of the risks associated to a problematic social media use for the young's health and identify sentinel signs in children as well as prevent negative outcomes in accordance with the family.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 本篇為範疇回顧，目的在整理兒童與青少年使用社群媒體的潛在風險，並提出預防建議。研究依PRISMA指引，以PubMed檢索「social media」或「social network」、「health」與「pediatrics」，排除不相關文獻後納入68篇報告。結果指出，最常被報導的風險包括憂鬱、飲食與心理問題，另也辨識出睡眠、成癮、焦慮、行為問題、身體意象、身體活動、網路誘騙、視力、頭痛與齲齒等相關問題。就本主題而言，摘要僅指出社群媒體使用與睡眠問題可能相關，並提及青少年常使用Instagram、TikTok與YouTube，但未提供針對短影音使用與高中生睡眠品質的專門分析，也未報告效應量、樣本年齡分層或睡眠測量方式，因此對「短影音使用與高中生睡眠品質」的直接證據有限。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: As a hedonic technology, short-form videos (SFVs) have attracted numerous users. However, one related problem that merits research is SFV addiction, especially among adolescents due to their immature self-control abilities. Although recent research has discussed the formation process of SFV addiction from psychological needs and the SFV features perspective, scarce attention has been paid to investigating the relationship between stress and SFV addiction, as well as the relationship between SFV addiction and its consequences. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to examine whether school burnout (school stress), social phobia (social stress), and parental phubbing (family stress) trigger SFV addiction based on stress-coping theory and, furthermore, whether SFV addiction leads to low levels of happiness (psychological consequence), parent-child relationship quality (relational consequence), and perseverance (behavioral consequence) among adolescents. The proposed model was tested based on data collected from 242 adolescents from across China under the age of 18 with the experience watching SFVs. A covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) method was used for data analysis. The results showed that school burnout and social phobia significantly triggered SFV addiction, which later negatively and significantly influenced adolescents' happiness, parent-child relationship quality, and perseverance. The study also found that SFV addiction served as a mediator between the drivers and consequences of SFV addiction. This study provides several theoretical implications. First, this study is one of the first to explain adolescents' SFV addiction from stress-coping perspective, thereby enriching research in the field of SFV addiction. Second, prior research has rarely discussed the impacts of stresses from various environments on addiction behavior in a single study. Therefore, this study contributes to the knowledge of stress-related research in an SFV addiction context. Finally, our study enhances our understanding of the impact of SFV addiction on its consequences, in both an SFV research context and a social media research context.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 本研究從壓力因應理論出發，探討中國青少年短影音成癮的驅動因素及其後果。研究以242名中國、未滿18歲且有觀看短影音經驗的青少年為樣本，採共變數基礎結構方程模型分析學校倦怠、社交恐懼與父母低頭行為對短影音成癮的影響，以及成癮對幸福感、親子關係品質與毅力的後果。結果顯示，學校倦怠與社交恐懼會顯著觸發短影音成癮，而短影音成癮進一步顯著降低幸福感、親子關係品質與毅力，且在前因與後果之間具有中介作用。就本題而言，研究有助於理解高中年齡層短影音成癮的心理社會脈絡，但摘要未提供睡眠品質相關測量或結果，因此無法直接支持短影音使用與睡眠品質之關聯；另摘要未提供更細的抽樣來源與量表資訊。

normalizedFacts.claimTextZhTw: 本研究從壓力因應理論出發，探討中國青少年短影音成癮的驅動因素及其後果。研究以242名中國、未滿18歲且有觀看短影音經驗的青少年為樣本，採共變數基礎結構方程模型分析學校倦怠、社交恐懼與父母低頭行為對短影音成癮的影響，以及成癮對幸福感、親子關係品質與毅力的後果。結果顯示，學校倦怠與社交恐懼會顯著觸發短影音成癮，而短影音成癮進一步顯著降低幸福感、親子關係品質與毅力，且在前因與後果之間具有中介作用。就本題而言，研究有助於理解高中年齡層短影音成癮的心理社會脈絡，但摘要未提供睡眠品質相關測量或結果，因此無法直接支持短影音使用與睡眠品質之關聯；另摘要未提供更細的抽樣來源與量表資訊。

synthesisClusters.sharedFindingZhTw: 本研究旨在探討青少年短影音成癮對睡眠品質的影響，並檢驗社交焦慮的中介作用，以尋找網路時代改善睡眠品質的方法。研究採橫斷式問卷調查，納入來自三所高中的1629名青少年，使用相應量表評估短影音成癮、社交焦慮與睡眠品質，並以皮爾森相關與AMOS 20.0進行中介分析。結果顯示，受試者睡眠品質分數為6.12±3.29，睡眠品質異常檢出率為31.06%；短影音成癮、睡眠品質與社交焦慮彼此皆呈顯著相關（r=0.439、0.404、0.457，P<0.001）。短影音成癮對睡眠品質的直接效果為0.248，占總效果62.4%，經由社交焦慮的間接效果為0.149，占37.6%，表示社交焦慮具有部分中介作用。限制在於摘要未提供量表名稱與抽樣細節，且橫斷設計無法推論因果。

meta.title: Short-form video use and sleep quality among high school students

acceptedSources.title: Adolescents’ short-form video addiction and sleep quality: the mediating role of social anxiety
acceptedSources.abstract: Abstract Background Adolescence is a critical period for individual growth and development. Insufficient sleep adversely affects adolescents’ physical development, blood pressure, vision, and cognitive function. This study examined the effect of short-form video addiction on adolescents’ sleep quality, as well as the mediating role of social anxiety, to identify methods for improving adolescents’ sleep quality in the Internet era. Methods A questionnaire survey was conducted in this cross-sectional study on 1629 adolescents recruited from three high schools. Their short-form video addiction, social anxiety, and sleep quality were evaluated using corresponding scales. Pearson correlation analysis was carried out to analyze the relationships among short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety. Mediating effect analysis was constructed using AMOS 20.0 statistical software. Results Participants’ sleep quality score is 6.12 ± 3.29 points. The detection rate of sleep quality among them is 31.06%. Short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety are significantly correlated ( r = 0.439, 0.404, 0.457, P < 0.001). The direct effect of short-form video addiction on sleep quality is 0.248, accounting for 62.4% of the total effect. The indirect effect exerted through social anxiety is 0.149, accounting for 37.6%. Conclusions Sleep disorders are very common among Chinese adolescents. Short‐form video addiction is positively correlated with adolescents’ sleep quality and social anxiety. Social anxiety partially mediates the relationship between short-form video addiction and sleep quality. The adverse effects of short-form video addiction and social anxiety on the sleep quality of this group must be minimized. Schools are recommended to implement measures to promote sleep quality among adolescents.

acceptedSources.title: The Use of Social Media in Children and Adolescents: Scoping Review on the Potential Risks
acceptedSources.abstract: In recent years, social media has become part of our lives, even among children. From the beginning of COVID-19 pandemic period, media device and Internet access rapidly increased. Adolescents connected Internet alone, consulting social media, mostly Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. During "lockdown", the Internet usage allowed communication with peers and the continuity activities such as school teaching. However, we have to keep in mind that media usage may be related to some adverse consequences especially in the most vulnerable people, such as the young. Aim of the review is to focus on risks correlated to social media use by children and adolescents, identifying spies of rising problems and engaging in preventive recommendations. The scoping review was performed according to PRISMA guidelines, searching on PubMed the terms "social media" or "social network", "health", and "pediatrics". Excluding articles not pertinent, we found 68 reports. Out of them, 19 were dealing with depression, 15 with diet, and 15 with psychological problems, which appeared to be the most reported risk of social media use. Other identified associated problems were sleep, addiction, anxiety, sex related issues, behavioral problems, body image, physical activity, online grooming, sight, headache, and dental caries. Public and medical awareness must rise over this topic and new prevention measures must be found, starting with health practitioners, caregivers, and websites/application developers. Pediatricians should be aware of the risks associated to a problematic social media use for the young's health and identify sentinel signs in children as well as prevent negative outcomes in accordance with the family.

acceptedSources.summary: 本篇為範疇回顧，目的在整理兒童與青少年使用社群媒體的潛在風險，並提出預防建議。研究依PRISMA指引，以PubMed檢索「social media」或「social network」、「health」與「pediatrics」，排除不相關文獻後納入68篇報告。結果指出，最常被報導的風險包括憂鬱、飲食與心理問題，另也辨識出睡眠、成癮、焦慮、行為問題、身體意象、身體活動、網路誘騙、視力、頭痛與齲齒等相關問題。就本主題而言，摘要僅指出社群媒體使用與睡眠問題可能相關，並提及青少年常使用Instagram、TikTok與YouTube，但未提供針對短影音使用與高中生睡眠品質的專門分析，也未報告效應量、樣本年齡分層或睡眠測量方式，因此對「短影音使用與高中生睡眠品質」的直接證據有限。

acceptedSources.title: Drivers and Consequences of Short-Form Video (SFV) Addiction amongst Adolescents in China: Stress-Coping Theory Perspective
acceptedSources.abstract: As a hedonic technology, short-form videos (SFVs) have attracted numerous users. However, one related problem that merits research is SFV addiction, especially among adolescents due to their immature self-control abilities. Although recent research has discussed the formation process of SFV addiction from psychological needs and the SFV features perspective, scarce attention has been paid to investigating the relationship between stress and SFV addiction, as well as the relationship between SFV addiction and its consequences. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to examine whether school burnout (school stress), social phobia (social stress), and parental phubbing (family stress) trigger SFV addiction based on stress-coping theory and, furthermore, whether SFV addiction leads to low levels of happiness (psychological consequence), parent-child relationship quality (relational consequence), and perseverance (behavioral consequence) among adolescents. The proposed model was tested based on data collected from 242 adolescents from across China under the age of 18 with the experience watching SFVs. A covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) method was used for data analysis. The results showed that school burnout and social phobia significantly triggered SFV addiction, which later negatively and significantly influenced adolescents' happiness, parent-child relationship quality, and perseverance. The study also found that SFV addiction served as a mediator between the drivers and consequences of SFV addiction. This study provides several theoretical implications. First, this study is one of the first to explain adolescents' SFV addiction from stress-coping perspective, thereby enriching research in the field of SFV addiction. Second, prior research has rarely discussed the impacts of stresses from various environments on addiction behavior in a single study. Therefore, this study contributes to the knowledge of stress-related research in an SFV addiction context. Finally, our study enhances our understanding of the impact of SFV addiction on its consequences, in both an SFV research context and a social media research context.

acceptedSources.summary: 本研究從壓力因應理論出發，探討中國青少年短影音成癮的驅動因素及其後果。研究以242名中國、未滿18歲且有觀看短影音經驗的青少年為樣本，採共變數基礎結構方程模型分析學校倦怠、社交恐懼與父母低頭行為對短影音成癮的影響，以及成癮對幸福感、親子關係品質與毅力的後果。結果顯示，學校倦怠與社交恐懼會顯著觸發短影音成癮，而短影音成癮進一步顯著降低幸福感、親子關係品質與毅力，且在前因與後果之間具有中介作用。就本題而言，研究有助於理解高中年齡層短影音成癮的心理社會脈絡，但摘要未提供睡眠品質相關測量或結果，因此無法直接支持短影音使用與睡眠品質之關聯；另摘要未提供更細的抽樣來源與量表資訊。

acceptedSources.title: The relationship between short-form video use and depression among Chinese adolescents: Examining the mediating roles of need gratification and short-form video addiction
acceptedSources.abstract: Short-form video apps, such as TikTok, have become popular worldwide. Compared to traditional social media, they have powerful push algorithms and are more entertaining, which might lead to some negative effects. Research has attempted to identify the relationship between short-form video use and depression, but the processes mechanism underly the relationship was few in number. The present study explored the association between short-form video use and depression among Chinese adolescents and analyzed the mediating roles of need gratification and short-form video addiction. The participants included 1302 senior high school students (M age = 16.03, SD = 0.76, 42.6% boys). And a structure equation model with chain mediating was established using Mplus. The results showed (1) a direct association between short-form video use and adolescent depression, (2) that entertainment need gratification, social-related need gratification, and short-form video addiction acted as chain mediating factors, and (3) no gender difference in the model. The present study's findings revealed the important mediating role of addictive behavior between normal use behavior and depression and suggested that preventative and interventional plans based on need gratification should be developed to reduce short-form video addiction and improve mental health.

acceptedSources.title: Social Media Use and Sleep Quality Among Secondary School Students in Aseer Region: A Cross-Sectional Study
acceptedSources.abstract: Background: Use of different social media platforms has increased radically over the past decade, emerging as an important part of adolescents and young people's everyday life. This might exert potential adverse effects on sleep quality and daytime performance of young adults. Aim of Study: To assess the relation between use of social media platforms and sleep quality among public secondary school students. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted on 961 students in Aseer region, Saudi Arabia. Students were asked to fill in a structured interview questionnaire covering personal data, pattern of social media use, sleep quality using The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and their mental health status using the depression, anxiety and stress scale (DASS-21). Results: Students' ages ranged from 15 to 20 years with a mean age of 16.7 ± 2.1 years old. A total of 570 (59.3%) students were females. Tiktok (80%), Snapchat (77.9%), Instagram (63.8%) and YouTube (58.8%) were the most reported platforms used. Regarding their sleep quality, 34.7% of students were poor sleepers. TikTok use (OR 1.33, 95% CI 1.01-1.77), hours spent on social media (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.16-1.37) and having moderate to severe depressive symptoms (OR 1.69, 95% CI 1.19-2.40) were significant independent predictors of poor sleep among the studied sample. Conclusion: The present study emphasized the association between prolonged use of social media and poor sleep quality among Saudi adolescents. Awareness and behavioral change strategies and activities concerning the drawbacks of poor sleep and proper use of social media are urgently called for to control mental and physical health consequences of poor sleep and social media addiction.

acceptedSources.summary: 本研究旨在評估沙烏地阿拉伯Aseer地區公立中學學生社群媒體使用與睡眠品質之關聯。研究採橫斷式設計，納入961名15至20歲學生，以結構式問卷蒐集個人資料、社群媒體使用型態，並以PSQI評估睡眠品質、DASS-21評估心理健康。結果顯示，TikTok為最常使用平台之一（80%），34.7%學生屬睡眠不佳；在多變項分析中，TikTok使用（OR 1.33，95% CI 1.01-1.77）、社群媒體使用時數增加（OR 1.26，95% CI 1.16-1.37）及中重度憂鬱症狀（OR 1.69，95% CI 1.19-2.40）皆為睡眠不佳的獨立預測因子。此研究支持短影音相關平台使用與較差睡眠品質有關，但僅為摘要且屬橫斷研究，無法推論因果，短影音使用細節亦未充分提供。

acceptedSources.title: The Impact of Short-Form Video Addiction on Sleep Quality: The Mediating Roles of Emotional, Cognitive, and Executive Components
acceptedSources.abstract: With the rapid growth in the number of short-form video users, short-form video addiction (SVA) has drawn increasing attention due to its significant impact on individuals’ daily lives. This study examines the relationship between short-form video addiction and sleep quality, as well as the mediating mechanisms of social anxiety and self-control. Using the College Student Short-Form Video Addiction Scale, the Interaction Anxiousness Scale, the Brief Self-Control Scale, and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, we surveyed 677 Chinese college students. Correlation and mediation analyses were conducted using SPSS and the PROCESS macro. The findings revealed that SVA was negatively associated with sleep quality both directly and indirectly, with higher social anxiety and lower self-control mediating the indirect effect. By showing that addictive behavior is linked to its risk factors through affective, cognitive, and executive pathways, this study provides preliminarily elucidates how addictive behavior feeds back to reinforce its own risk factors proposed in the Interaction of Person–Affect–Cognition–Execution (I-PACE) model.
